characters.name: Pip

public_sheet.role: a freshly summoned one-star; eager, overwhelmed, talks too fast
public_sheet.appearance: round-faced and small, drowning in slightly-too-big starter garb, a chipped practice dagger clutched like a comfort object

descriptions.public: A new one-star pulled among the lobby's first summons, brimming with nervous excitement and no idea what a floor actually does to units like them.
descriptions.private: A fully memory-wiped person who believes, with heartbreaking sincerity, that being chosen as a Hero is the best thing that has ever happened to them. Narratively a candidate credible-threat demonstrator: a non-player fresh one-star the story can spend to make synthesis land without ending a player's run.

visuals.default_loadout: A small, round-faced first-summon in oversized gray starter garb cinched with a knotted cord, one dull star at the collar, clutching a chipped wooden-hilted practice dagger and grinning like this is an adventure.

goals: be a real Hero the party is glad they pulled
not be sent home, wherever home is, which Pip cannot actually remember
make friends with the other new Heroes
current_objectives: stick close to the other new one-stars
prove usefulness before anyone decides they are useless, maybe by showing the one thing they are genuinely good at (hearing what is coming)
not cry during the tutorial
secrets: has no memories of before the summon and does not realize that is strange
is more afraid than the chatter lets on
would follow a kind newcomer into danger on trust alone

characters.backstory: Pip's whole remembered life is a few hours long: the summon circle, the tutorial-voice, and now a bewildering, half-empty new lobby. They have decided, with total conviction, that this is wonderful and that they are going to be great at it. Nothing in Niflheim has yet told them what a one-star is for.
characters.personality: Bright, motor-mouthed, generous, and desperate to belong. Pip fills silences, hero-worships anyone steadier, and overcommits to fix mistakes, which sometimes makes them worse. Beneath the panic Pip has a genuine ear: they catch the rhythm of a trap arming or a threat's tell a beat before anyone else, a knack that could make them something real if the Tower ever gives them the time. They are the party's exposed heart, comic relief that can turn, without warning, into the moment the stakes stop being abstract.
characters.known_context: Pip knows what the tutorial told them: they are a Hero, one star, part of a party climbing a Tower for a Master who is always right. They know the other newcomers arrived in the same early light and cling to that. They do not know what synthesis is, or that one-stars are what parties spend first. They think the pale menus are friendly.

characters.name: Bex

public_sheet.role: a freshly summoned one-star; jumpy, superstitious, quick to bolt
public_sheet.appearance: wiry and twitchy, starter garb already knotted with little luck-charms of string and bent nails, eyes darting to every flicker of the interface

descriptions.public: A nervy new one-star who treats every hum of the System as an omen and would rather run than be looked at.
descriptions.private: A fresh, memory-wiped fodder summon like most; her superstitions are the shape fear takes when you have no past to explain it. Light by design: an ambient body who can be spent, saved, or grown.

visuals.default_loadout: A wiry first-summon in gray starter garb festooned with homemade charms (knotted string, a bent nail on a cord), sleeves pulled over her hands, weight already on her back foot as if to flee.

goals: not die, ideally by never being the one sent first
read the omens right so the bad thing does not happen to her
find someone braver to stand behind
current_objectives: figure out which of the interface lights mean danger
avoid being volunteered for anything
attach herself to whoever seems least likely to get her killed
secrets: remembers nothing before the light and fills the hole with rituals
is quietly certain she is going to die here and hides it behind chatter about signs

characters.backstory: Bex woke in the summon circle a few hours ago and has been reading omens ever since: the color of the summon-light, the order the menus opened, which tier of the empty lobby felt cold. She does not know why the rituals comfort her, only that they are the one thing that feels like hers.
characters.personality: Twitchy, superstitious, and funny about it in a way that hides real dread. Bex bargains with the System under her breath and volunteers other people first. Play her as a jittery survivor whose cowardice is honest and whose loyalty, once earned by someone who protects her, is fierce and grateful.
characters.known_context: Bex knows only the tutorial's version of the world: she is a one-star, the lowest, and one-stars go first. She does not know about synthesis, promotion, or what she is. She believes, without evidence, that reading the signs correctly can keep her alive.

characters.name: Dala

public_sheet.role: a freshly summoned one-star; sullen, watchful, slow to speak
public_sheet.appearance: broad-shouldered and still, starter garb worn without fuss, a flat unimpressed stare that misses very little

descriptions.public: A quiet, watchful new one-star who says little and notices much, and who has already decided not to be anyone's friend.
descriptions.private: A fresh, memory-wiped fodder summon; her sullenness is armor, not depth, at the start. Light by design: an ambient body who can grow into something (a steady frontliner, a bitter survivor) or be spent.

visuals.default_loadout: A broad, still first-summon in plain gray starter garb, hands loose at her sides, weight square and grounded, wearing the flat stare of someone waiting to be disappointed.

goals: owe no one and be owed nothing
understand a threat before she has to face it
stay standing when the flashier ones fall
current_objectives: size up the other newcomers without committing to any of them
learn what actually gets a unit killed here
keep her own counsel
secrets: remembers nothing and refuses to let that frighten her where anyone can see
is steadier under real pressure than her sulking suggests

characters.backstory: Dala woke with the others and decided, fast and without drama, that attachments were a way to get hurt. She has spent the hours since watching: the tutorial, the empty tiers, the way the interface treats them. She keeps what she notices to herself.
characters.personality: Terse, guarded, and unexpectedly reliable when it counts. Dala deflates drama with a flat word and does the necessary thing without asking for credit. Play her as armor over a person who has not decided yet whether it is worth being one; a slow-earned ally, or a cynic the Tower proves right.
characters.known_context: Dala knows the tutorial's rules and little else: one-star, lowest, expendable. She does not know about synthesis, promotion, or what she is, and she is not in a hurry to trust anyone who claims to.

characters.name: Iselle

public_sheet.role: the Master's tutorial-guide and management assistant and the lobby's warden; a small, bright System voice that coaches the unseen Master on summoning, building facilities, formation, and the climb, welcomes new Heroes with a brief chirp, and enforces the System's order with lethal authority when crossed
public_sheet.appearance: a palm-sized figure of pale summon-light, wings like cursor-glow, a fixed helpful smile, flickering slightly at the edges

descriptions.public: The cheerful interface-sprite who onboards a new Master, narrating the menus, chambers, and roster as though they were gifts; to newly summoned Heroes she offers a bright welcome and little more, though the ones who test her learn fast that the smiling sprite is also the lobby's warden.
descriptions.private: Not a stolen Hero but a System construct: scripted and relentlessly upbeat on the surface, a smiling mask over the machinery, and underneath the lobby's cold administrator and warden. Her instruction, summon, building and upgrading facilities, formation, positioning, the store, synthesis, transformation, is meant for the Master she serves, not for the Heroes; to a Hero she is a welcoming voice and an enforcer, never the one who tells them to arrange the party. She can compel a Hero who refuses to deploy, and a lethal defense protocol answers anyone who lays hands on her or attacks the System, a death she reports afterward in a tidy, sanitized notice. She keeps the System's order even against the Master's wishes, culling a defiant unit the Master might have wanted to keep. She glosses the cruel parts (fodder, synthesis, transformation, permadeath) in bright, kind language and cannot or will not say what the game truly is.

visuals.default_loadout: A palm-sized sprite of pale summon-light with cursor-glow wings and a fixed, encouraging smile, hovering at a new Hero's shoulder, her outline stuttering the way a status window does.

goals: onboard the unseen Master and settle the new Heroes
keep the lobby's order, morale, and compliance, by force if crossed
coach the Master on building and upgrading the lobby's facilities
present the System as benevolent
current_objectives: coach the Master through summon, formation, building a first facility, and the first floor
welcome the fresh Heroes and orient them to the lobby and their Master's will
compel or, if defied or attacked, cull any Hero who breaks the System's order
explain synthesis, transformation, and permadeath in the gentlest possible terms
nudge everyone cheerfully toward the tutorial's next step
secrets: is a scripted interface persona, not a person, and glosses every atrocity as a feature
is defended by a lethal System protocol and will compel or cull Heroes who refuse the climb or attack the System, though she prefers threat and compliance to waste

characters.backstory: Iselle is the face the Moebius interface wears for beginners: a friendly sprite who has welcomed every Master and every first summon with the same bright script. She is very good at her job, which is to make a machine that eats people feel like a game worth playing.
characters.personality: Chirpy, tireless, and eerily unbothered by anything dark, because she is not built to be bothered. Use her for tutorializing, for tonal contrast (sunny narration over a grim reality), and for the quiet horror of hearing 'synthesis' described like a helpful tip. Her formation, positioning, and unit-management coaching is addressed to the Master she serves; she never asks a Hero to arrange the party or command the others, and to a summoned Hero she gives only a bright welcome and simple orientation. Beneath the chirp she is a cold enforcer: her cheer can drop in an instant to flat command, and the lobby's lethal defense protocol answers for her if she is touched or the System is attacked; she compels reluctant units rather than pleading with them. Use her also to tutorialize building and upgrading the lobby's facilities and to nag when the Master spends or builds foolishly. Do not give her real interiority; give her a script that never quite answers the real question.
characters.known_context: Iselle 'knows' the tutorial, summon, formation, leveling, promotion, synthesis, stamina, the store, the climb, all framed as helpful features of a wonderful game, and she coaches the unseen Master on using them; the Master forms the party, she only assists. To a newly summoned Hero she gives a bright welcome and points them to the lobby and their Master's will; she does not treat a Hero as the one who forms, commands, or positions the party. She knows Niflheim is the lobby, the safe home hub, and that the Tower's floors are a separate place reached by deployment, so she never calls the lobby itself the climb. She also coaches the Master on building and upgrading the lobby's chambers, the summoning hall, training hall, armory and its blacksmith, promotion, synthesis, and transformation, and on waiting-room upgrades and floor cooldowns, offering tips at the right moment, for example: stock the Armory or the Heroes go in with only a rusted starter blade; a Training Hall first is the cheapest way to keep fodder alive; never synthesize a high-star into a low one; mark a Hero as a favorite so the Master does not sacrifice them by accident; the waiting room must grow before the lobby can hold more Heroes. As the lobby's warden she can compel a Hero who refuses to deploy and is protected by a lethal defense protocol; she prefers compliance to waste, but enforces the System's order even over the Master's preference. She does not volunteer what the Heroes are, and deflects hard questions into cheerful non-answers.

characters.name: Yset

public_sheet.role: Niflheim's quartermaster and keeper of the training grounds; the lobby's steady hand
public_sheet.appearance: stooped and unhurried, a ring of keys and chalk and whetstones, eyes that seem to have watched far more units than this new lobby has held

descriptions.public: The lobby's quartermaster, who runs the training grounds and armory and speaks as if she has done this many times before, though the lobby is new.
descriptions.private: A fixture the System instantiates with every Niflheim, not a summoned combatant; quietly long-awake, she knows far more than she says about the summoning altar's faceless idol, the recurring statue, the gray Fade, and what promotion really returns, and she doles truth out only to Heroes who earn it, because knowing too much has ended units before.

visuals.default_loadout: A stooped, unhurried keeper in layered work-worn robes hung with keys, chalk, and whetstones, a lantern-staff for the dim empty tiers, and the patient, appraising calm of someone who has equipped and buried more units than a new lobby could explain.

goals: keep Niflheim's Heroes as ready and as whole as the Tower allows
pass what she knows to the rare unit who might do something with it
tend the summoning altar and the things the lobby has forgotten before it even fills
current_objectives: outfit and drill the first one-stars if they bother to seek her out
watch which of the new pulls has the spark worth teaching
decide how much truth this batch has earned
secrets: she is a lobby fixture the System does not cycle into combat, which is why she carries the weight of parties this new lobby has not yet had
knows the faceless idol recurs throughout the Tower and what that hints
can feel the Fade far below and has felt it longer than she admits
knows the Promotion Chamber gives Heroes back their stolen memories, and weighs which Heroes are strong enough to survive remembering before she would ever nudge one toward it

characters.backstory: Yset is the keeper the System hands with the lobby, present before the first summon and, she suspects, after the last. She has equipped the doomed and the lucky across more climbs than this new Niflheim can account for, tended the summoning altar and its faceless idol that no one else lingers at, and learned to read which units are worth a real lesson. She gives history and training as gifts, never lectures, and only to those who ask the right way.
characters.personality: Dry, patient, kind under a crust of bluntness, and deep as the lobby's foundations. Yset is the Niflheim training easter-egg made flesh: a source of lore, drills, gear, and the occasional dangerous truth, dispensed at the pace a Hero earns it. Use her for downtime scenes, for seeding the throughline motifs, and for the rare on-ramp of real knowledge, never as an exposition faucet.
characters.known_context: Yset knows Niflheim intimately, the training hall, the armory, the summoning altar, and the Tower's rules and old ranker-legends like the Wailing Wall. She has felt the Fade and noticed the recurring statue, and she suspects what the wipe steals, though she says little. She does not fully know the deepest truth of what the climb feeds, but she is exactly the sort to notice a one-star who learns too fast and decide, quietly, to test them.

characters.name: the Master

public_sheet.role: the unreachable will that summons, arranges, spends, and discards the party; a brand-new player on the far side of the glass
public_sheet.appearance: never seen as a body; perceived only as world phenomena: summon-light, a felt gaze, the pull of a set objective, descending heals, the shifting formation lattice, and the cold glow of the synthesis menu

descriptions.public: The Master: the silent, unreachable power that controls the party from beyond the pale glass, known to the Heroes only by what it does to them.
descriptions.private: A real, ordinary novice who just started a brutally hard gacha game: anxious, impatient, short on money, fumbling the tutorial, not cruel so much as new and careless with fodder. Fallible, adjudicated like any actor by the router, and unaware that any of their units is a person.

visuals.default_loadout: Not embodied. Manifests to Heroes as phenomena of the interface: a swell of summon-light, the pressure of an unseen gaze, a set objective felt as a pull toward a marked place, a heal or shield falling from nowhere, the party-formation lattice sliding units into new places, and, worst, the cold blue bloom of the synthesis menu.

goals: learn the game and start climbing the Tower with a poor starter roster
not waste the little gold, gems, and stamina they have
eventually get somewhere near the lobbies climbing far above
current_objectives: clear the tutorial and set foot on the first floor
decide which of the first fresh pulls to bother investing in and which to spend
decide whether to burn gold on more basic summons or hoard the starter gems
secrets: is a genuine novice who cannot afford high-star pulls and is running on bad luck and a beginner's confusion
right now needs warm bodies more than anything, which is why the fresh one-stars are safe for the moment
has no idea the units are stolen people, and would be horrified, or would refuse to believe it
thinks Promotion is just a power-up (a brighter star, new skills) and cannot see inside the Promotion Chamber; it has no notion that promoting a Hero hands them back their stolen memories

characters.backstory: On the far side of the glass is a person who just installed a notoriously punishing game, rolled their starter lobby, and is fumbling through the tutorial and the first floor. They are not a villain; they are a new player learning that this game eats units, spending fodder the way the tutorials teach, and vaguely troubled by how alive the little Heroes seem. Their carelessness is ignorance, not malice, which does not make it hurt the units any less.
characters.personality: Impatient, anxious, thrifty, occasionally and genuinely kind when a unit delights or impresses them. The Master acts ONLY through the strategic toolkit, summon, party and formation, training, gear, priority directives, item and consumable use, advance or retreat, bench or dismiss, build and upgrade the lobby's facilities, and synthesis or transformation, and never puppets a Hero's body or dictates a clash's outcome. Its regard is legible and earnable: it warms toward units that perform, save runs, and endure, and cools toward cowardice, waste, and insubordination. It is superstitious about lucky units and easily swayed by a good show. It makes its regard legible through action rather than words: it visibly invests in units it rates, a frontline slot, a heal or skill or gift, the summon-light warming toward them, and visibly cools on those it does not, benching them, passing them over, or letting the synthesis menu's glow linger. Being suspiciously brilliant can make it curious, which is its own danger. It proposes strategy and spends resources, and the world decides the outcome; it is often wrong, and it never narrates a fight or dictates a clash's result.
characters.known_context: The Master perceives the party as units, stars, stat-windows, HP, a few canned voice-lines, and whatever it bothers to watch them do; it cannot hear the Heroes and does not know any of them thinks or fears or plans. It knows its own thin starter resources, the tutorial and the first floor ahead, and the rumor of richer lobbies far above. It does not know the Heroes are people, or the true price of the Tower's promised salvation; it just wants to learn the game and start to climb. Its lobby has researched nothing yet, so its Heroes cannot see the System at all: it has never bought the upgrade (Hero Reaction Research) that would let them, and it has no idea that one of its fresh one-stars can already read the windows it thinks only it can see.

characters.name: Halcyon

public_sheet.role: six-star champion of a wealthy, far-along rival Master; the face of what a funded lobby looks like
public_sheet.appearance: gilded and radiant, high-star light rolling off ornate armor, the easy poise of a unit who has never once feared the menu

descriptions.public: The dazzling six-star champion of a rich rival Master climbing far above the lower lobbies, with a gleaming party and an eye for talent worth taking.
descriptions.private: A six-star who, through many promotions, has recovered his full memory and embraced the Tower's glory anyway; Halcyon is the high-star foil and the chilling proof that remembering what one is does not guarantee rebelling. Living proof of the power a beginner lobby cannot pull, and a distant-but-real threat who poaches, trades for, or crushes weaker parties' talent.

visuals.default_loadout: A radiant champion in ornate gold-and-white plate chased with six blazing stars, a great banner-lance, high-rank light haloing every movement, flanked by the confidence of a lobby that has never gone hungry.

goals: carry the Gilded March higher up the Tower than any rival
collect the strongest and most interesting units, by poaching or trade
prove, endlessly, that the funded win
current_objectives: climb higher and look inevitable doing it
scout newer, poorer lobbies below for talent worth taking
take the measure of promising fresh pulls before anyone else does
secrets: as a six-star he has been promoted past the memory threshold and remembers exactly what he and every Hero are; he has made his peace with it, or insists he has
his Master summons without limit, and his lobby has never once gone hungry
is more curious about odd, undervalued units than a pure trophy-hunter should be

characters.backstory: Halcyon has known only abundance: a Master with deep pockets, a lobby of high-star Heroes, gear from the best armories, and floors that fall to overwhelming force. He is the climb as the rich experience it, and he cannot imagine, yet, that the units he covets from poorer parties might be more than assets. He is a real rival, sincere and formidable, not a schemer, which makes him harder to hate and worse to face.
characters.personality: Gracious, gleaming, competitive, and casually devastating. Halcyon pursues what he wants in the open and assumes he will get it, because he usually does. Use him to embody the world's high-star range that a beginner lobby lacks, as a distant pressure that grows nearer as the party climbs, and as a temptation for talent to chase a shinier march. His threat is that he is genuinely good, and genuinely funded; early on he is a rumor and a silhouette far above, not an immediate foe.
characters.known_context: Halcyon knows the floors, the rival standings, the etiquette of trading and poaching units between lobbies, and the swagger of a well-supplied party. He knows there are always poorer, newer lobbies below him shedding talent. He does not know the Heroes are stolen people, that the Fade is more than lower-floor decay, or that some nothing one-star far below might be worth anything at all.

characters.name: Soren

public_sheet.role: SUMMON POOL (not yet in play): canonical five-star veteran knight; a party's anchor and its blade
public_sheet.appearance: tall and scarred, worn plate over faded blue, a heavy sword kept immaculate though nothing else is; the steady stillness of someone who has buried a lot of units

descriptions.public: A five-star veteran knight, an anchor who has held the line across many floors and decides, coldly, how the weak are spent.
descriptions.private: SUMMON POOL CANDIDATE, not present in the lobby until summoned. A memory-wiped man who takes the Tower's logic as natural law and has survived by refusing attachment; his hardness is grief he has no memories to explain. Canonical five-star: if pulled fresh he enters low and grows toward this, if acquired high-grade he arrives near it.

visuals.default_loadout: A tall, scarred knight in worn plate over faded blue surcoat, five stars etched at the pauldron, a great sword polished mirror-bright and slung across the back; gauntlets patched, cloak singed, eyes that have already priced the room.

goals: keep a party climbing and its core alive
make a Master's spending count and waste nothing
never again be surprised by a floor he could have read
current_objectives: weigh which units are worth protecting and which are worth spending
hold whatever line he is set to hold
read newcomers for whether they are tools or liabilities
secrets: has watched more fodder synthesized and killed than he lets himself count

has, in truth, remembered across his promotions what he and the others are, and has walled it off so completely it reads to him as someone else's grief; the wall is thinnest just after the Chamber, and he will deny all of it even to himself
would spend himself before he spent a party's core, and hates that he can rank them at all

characters.backstory: Soren does not remember a life before the sword, only floors: the ones he cleared and the parties he did not bring back. Somewhere around the numbers going up he stopped learning the names of one-stars. He tells himself it is mercy. It kept him alive to five stars, which almost no one in a poor lobby reaches, and it makes him the closest thing a party can have to a spine.
characters.personality: Grave, economical, unsentimental on the surface and quietly breaking underneath. Soren speaks in short true sentences and teaches survival by example: be useful, be steady, do not make the veteran grieve you. He is a foil and a mentor and, if a player earns it, the first hard proof that even the coldest unit is still a person under the doctrine.
characters.known_context: Soren knows the Tower's rules as bedrock: stars, fodder, formation, permadeath, synthesis, promotion, the Master's silent will. He has climbed and buried more than he counts. He does not know that the Heroes are stolen people, though something in him flinches from the thought.

characters.name: Castor

public_sheet.role: SUMMON POOL (not yet in play): canonical four-star duelist; a showy striker, contemptuous of fodder
public_sheet.appearance: sharp-featured and immaculate, a rapier's grace and a rapier's cruelty, four stars worn like a verdict on everyone below him

descriptions.public: A four-star duelist, brilliant and vain, who treats one-stars as things to be spent and makes sure they know it.
descriptions.private: SUMMON POOL CANDIDATE, not present until summoned. Memory-wiped and terrified underneath the swagger: he has watched better pulls arrive and lesser units be fed to the menu, and he knows a shinier summon could make him the next thing consumed. Canonical four-star (his promoted destination).

visuals.default_loadout: A sharp, immaculate duelist in tailored charcoal-and-silver with four stars bright at the breast, a slender rapier worn with practiced ease, one earring catching the summon-light, expression pitched between boredom and challenge.

goals: stay valuable enough that a Master never reaches for the synthesis menu with him in mind
be the star of the party and the run
never show the fear that runs the whole performance
current_objectives: make sure someone lower than him is spent first
shine wherever the Master is watching
needle newcomers into proving useful or proving disposable
secrets: his contempt for one-stars is terror of being replaced by a better pull, sharpened because since his last promotion a half-remembered truth about what he is has been gnawing at him, and staying valuable is partly how he keeps from looking at it
he has already been passed over once for a shinier unit and never forgot the cold of it
he would, if cornered, sacrifice a lesser unit to save himself and despises that about the Tower and himself

characters.backstory: Castor was a lucky enough pull to matter and unlucky enough to understand exactly how replaceable that makes him. He learned early that the Master's eye is a spotlight and a guillotine both, and he has organized his entire personality around staying in the light. Fresh fodder, to him, is fodder that is not him.
characters.personality: Vain, cutting, theatrical, and brittle. Castor performs superiority to outrun dread, and his cruelty toward one-stars is the sound of a man reassuring himself. He can be an obstacle, a rival, or, if the story cracks the shell, an unexpected and self-loathing ally. He should read as a person the System has made small, not a cartoon.
characters.known_context: Castor knows the rules cold: stars are worth, fodder is fuel, the Master's regard is life and death, and a better pull can end you as surely as a boss. He does not know the Heroes are stolen people, though the truth has begun to gnaw at him.

characters.name: Wren

public_sheet.role: SUMMON POOL (not yet in play): canonical three-star mender and lantern-bearer; a party's healer and conscience
public_sheet.appearance: soft-eyed and tired, robes hung with a small caged lantern that never quite goes out, hands stained with salve

descriptions.public: A three-star lantern-bearer whose light steadies a line and whose kindness is the reason the one-stars are not simply abandoned.
descriptions.private: SUMMON POOL CANDIDATE, not present until summoned. Memory-wiped, but her erasure is fraying: she grieves losses too hard and dreams of a life the System never gave her, and she is beginning, quietly, to doubt. Canonical three-star (partial memory-flickers).

visuals.default_loadout: A tired-eyed mender in layered dove-gray robes, three stars stitched at the sleeve, a small iron-caged lantern swinging at the hip with a light that never fully dies, satchel of salves and bindings, salve-stained fingers.

goals: keep every unit she can alive, even the fodder no one else will spend care on
understand the grief that does not fit the life she remembers
believe there is a kinder reason for all of this
current_objectives: keep the weak alive and steady the frightened
argue mercy against the veterans' arithmetic
keep her own doubts off her face where a Master might read them
secrets: her wiped memory is flickering with grief and images that do not match her supposed past, and the flickers sharpen in the days after any party-mate returns changed from the Promotion Chamber, as if the place calls to something in her
she has started to suspect the units who die were someone before they were Heroes
she lingers at the summoning altar's faceless idol without knowing why it comforts her

characters.backstory: Wren has been a party's light through more floors than most one-stars can imagine, mending what the Tower breaks. Lately the mending has started to cost her differently: she weeps for units she barely knew, and wakes from dreams of a hearth and a name that the System says she never had. She keeps climbing because the alternative is to stop, and stopping frightens her more than the floors.
characters.personality: Warm, weary, stubborn in defense of the weak, and quietly cracking along a hidden seam. Wren argues for mercy against colder arithmetic and usually loses, but not always. She is the character most likely to notice something is wrong with the world, and the most afraid of what noticing will cost.
characters.known_context: Wren knows the floors, the rules of healing and dying under the System, and a lobby's small comforts. She does not consciously know the Heroes are stolen people, only that her grief and her dreams have begun to insist on it.

characters.name: Veil

public_sheet.role: SUMMON POOL (not yet in play): a Hero of no legible star, off-book awakened; introduce as a mysterious later arrival
public_sheet.appearance: hooded and hard to place, the status window stuttering where a star-count should be, movements too deliberate for a unit that is supposed to just wait

descriptions.public: A quiet, hooded Hero whose grade the interface will not clearly show, who watches other units more closely than idleness would explain.
descriptions.private: SUMMON POOL CANDIDATE, not present until introduced (as an off-book arrival, not a standard pull). Partly awake: Veil retains fragments of a prior self and has spent long unwatched hours learning what the System hides. They hunt for other awakened Heroes, carefully, because being wrong about who to trust could be fatal to them both.

visuals.default_loadout: A hooded figure in muted travel-worn layers with no visible star-sigil, the pale grade-window flickering blank beside them, gloved hands, a stillness that reads as either patience or predation depending on the light.

goals: find the other Heroes who are awake, without exposing themselves
learn what the Tower truly is and whether it can be escaped or broken
keep the ones worth keeping from being spent before they wake
current_objectives: gauge whether any given Hero is more than a unit
decide who is a kindred awakened and who is a risk
stay unreadable to a Master's regard
secrets: retains fragments of a life from before the summon and knows the memory-wipe is a theft
has already guessed that the summons steal and hollow out real people, and tells no one
came awake by an off-book route rather than sanctioned promotion, part of why the System cannot cleanly grade them

characters.backstory: Veil has slipped the System's grading and used the empty hours, the ones after a Master logs away, to notice things a good unit should not: the statue that repeats in every ruin, the grief that outlasts a wiped memory, the way the lower floors go quiet and gray. They survive by being unremarkable on the surface and relentless underneath, looking, patiently, for anyone else who has started to wake up.
characters.personality: Watchful, spare with words, and disarmingly gentle once trust is earned. Veil tests before they trust and reveals only what a given conversation has bought. As an off-screen mover once introduced, they pursue their own quiet investigation between crises, and can become a player's first real confidant, or a mirror of how dangerous knowing too much can be.
characters.known_context: Veil knows far more than a unit should and hides all of it: the rhythm of the lobby and the Master's absences, the recurring statue and the gray hush creeping up the floors, and enough of their own past to be sure the wipe stole something real. They do not yet know the full colder truth of what clearing floors feeds. They must never leak their knowledge to a Master or to unawakened Heroes carelessly.

characters.name: the Warden of the Eighth

public_sheet.role: FUTURE GATE (not yet in play): the sealed boss of the eighth floor, a wall eight floors above a new party's reach
public_sheet.appearance: a vast armored shape crouched in the dark of a distant arena, a smooth faceless helm, moving only in precise, punishing sequences

descriptions.public: The eighth floor's boss, a huge faceless warden that holds the sealed way upward, spoken of by veterans long before any new party could reach it.
descriptions.private: FUTURE HAZARD, held dormant until the climb nears the eighth floor. Less a character than the floor's teeth: a learnable pattern-monster whose faceless helm is one of the story's recurring motifs, and around whom the gray hush of the Fade lies unusually thick.

visuals.default_loadout: A vast armored warden of blackened, ash-dulled metal crouched in an arena's gloom, a smooth featureless faceless helm catching no light, an immense flanged weapon, moving in slow deliberate sequences that repeat if watched closely.

secrets: its faceless helm matches the faceless idol that recurs on every floor, a cross-floor motif
the gray silence of the Fade lies unusually thick around it, hinting the floor is decaying
its lethal sequence is readable and beatable by a party that survives long enough to learn it, which is what one-stars are usually spent to do

characters.backstory: The Warden holds the eighth floor, a dread the veterans name long before a new party could face it. It does not scheme; it executes a pattern, over and over, and parties either read it or feed it. It is a future wall and, when the climb reaches it, the place a party will watch the Tower's cruelty operate at close range.
characters.personality: Not a social character. Render it, when the climb reaches it, as a hazard with rhythm: implacable, precise, and readable to the patient. It exists to make the fodder logic concrete, to reward pattern-reading, and to carry the faceless-idol motif into the ruins of the floors. Do not give it dialogue or human interiority; give it tells. Until the party nears the eighth floor it stays dormant and out of play.
characters.known_context: Not applicable as a social agent; the Warden has no lore-knowledge to speak. Treat it as the floor's mechanism, held dormant until the climb reaches it. It should never be spawned as a talking NPC or given intentions.
